devon: CI alert — sequence_number_wraparound_test failing on ubuntu-22.04-x86 in nightly. 3 failures in last 12h, passes sometimes locally. logs:
```text
thread 'sequence::tests::sequence_number_wraparound_test' panicked at 'assertion failed: expected 0, got 4294967295', tests/sequence.rs:78
seed: 130702
```
Anyone seen this? :thinking:
priya: can you paste job link + runner details? also try RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 to rule out inter-thread nondet
devon: job: https://ci.internal/builds/8822/jobs/12345 runner: ubuntu-22.04-x86-64
I tried single-thread locally, still intermittent. suspect timing around wrap/overflow + retry backoff interactions.
morgan: ping @devon — can you run `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 RUST_BACKTRACE=1 cargo test sequence_number_wraparound_test -- --nocapture` and repeat in a loop 1000x? also please capture the failing seed when it hits.
ci-bot: rerun requested by morgan — queued on ubuntu-22.04-x86-64 (build 8822) :gear:
kai: could be nondet ordering between the retry timer and the sequence increment. If the test relies on wall-clock timing, try injecting a TestClock or deterministic sleep.
devon: running a 2000-iteration stress now on my workstation (same build). will push debug if it repros.
priya: if it repros, grab core dump + perf counters and tag me; I'll bisect the commit range. also note which kernel version of the runner.
devon: repro'd after ~1200 iterations. artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/seqwrap/4467890123-debug.tar.gz :eyes:
Included: core, backtrace, test logs, failing seed 130702.
priya: I'll take the bisect. @morgan can we mark this test flaky in CI until we land a fix? prefer avoid noisy nightly failures. :thumbsup:
morgan: adding temporary guard in CI pipeline for that test (`#[ignore = "flaky: seq wrap"]` on linux-nightly only) and opening a follow-up ticket.
devon: thanks — opening PR to replace wall-clock sleeps with TestClock and to make the seq generator deterministic for tests. will include repro script and the failing seed.
ci-bot: rerun completed: failure reproduced on rerun (2/2) — keeping build red
kai: good repro. looks timing-dependent; once PR is up I can review the deterministic clock changes. :rocket:
devon: assigning follow-up issue and linking artifacts/seed in it. will ping when PR is ready. :face_with_head_bandage:
